target_customer: Parents, children aged about 5 to 14 and teachers buying or downloading single-subject learning apps on iPhone and iPad
problem: Children's learning apps were often cluttered; Tap to Learn built simple apps that each focus on one area of learning with interactivity and game elements.
business_model: Consumer mobile apps sold or free per app in the App Store

founders.name: Roby Thomas John
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

founders.name: Avinash Pandey
founders.background_notes: YC page says Tap to Learn was an earlier startup and he is now CTO at LILA Games.

founders.name: Aamir Poonawalla
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; the bio shown there describes later work, so it is not recorded as prior.

founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Simple iOS educational games built with standard tools; the work was content and design volume rather than hard engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Educational app mechanics were easy to copy and the App Store had many kids apps, so only content quality and chart rankings differentiated it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the company. Its own site still described it as a game studio with 36 million downloads.

market_need_then: The company's own site says its Grammar App was featured as Apple New and Noteworthy and other titles reached the top 20 Education charts in 20 plus countries, which shows downloads demand, though not the dates.

branding.domain_note: taptolearn.com is the company domain per the YC page and the live site.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found. The name is a plain description and is shared with unrelated apps such as Tap and Learn, so it is easy to confuse.

outcome_analysis: The YC directory marks Tap to Learn Inactive with no date or cause, and no shutdown or acquisition report was found. The company website is live and describes a studio founded in 2011 with over 50 apps and 36 million downloads that is rebuilding titles for the web, so the cause of the Inactive label is not public and may reflect a change of business rather than a failure.
notes: Funding rests on aggregators only. CB Insights reports roughly 40 thousand dollars across four rounds with the latest a seed of about 20 thousand in December 2012; that single database figure is recorded as one round. Dealroom claims over 1 million dollars from YC investors, which conflicts and is unverified. The live site conflicts with the Inactive status. No dated competitor sources existed; competitor searches returned only current app listings, so the list is empty. YC page shows five founders against a team size of 11.
